title: How volcanoes work
text: hey guys welcome back so today we are going to the volcano unit which honestly is my favourite unit of the whole year so a volcano is basically an opening in the earth's crust where molten rock gas and ash escape from deep inside the planet and to understand why that happens we need to look at what is under our feet the earth has layers there is the thin solid crust on top then the mantle which is hot rock that can flow very slowly and then the core in the middle now deep in the mantle and lower crust the rock melts and becomes magma magma is molten rock that is underground and because it is lighter than the solid rock around it it rises up through cracks and collects in a magma chamber under the volcano once magma comes out onto the surface we call it lava so same stuff different name depending on where it is lava can be really hot like seven hundred to twelve hundred degrees celsius which is hotter than any oven in your kitchen ok so why does it erupt the magma contains dissolved gases mostly water vapour and carbon dioxide and as the magma rises the pressure drops and the gas comes out as bubbles kind of like when you open a shaken bottle of soda the pressure builds and builds until the magma bursts out through the vent that is an eruption by the way i once tried the soda thing in class and it went all over the ceiling so do not do that one at home not every eruption is the same though if the magma is runny and has little gas you get gentle eruptions with rivers of lava like in hawaii but if the magma is thick and sticky and full of gas the gas cannot escape easily and you get explosive eruptions that blast ash and rock high into the sky like mount st helens in nineteen eighty most volcanoes are found where tectonic plates meet the plates are huge pieces of the crust that move a few centimetres a year where one plate sinks under another the rock melts and forms magma and there is a ring of volcanoes around the pacific ocean called the ring of fire some volcanoes like hawaii form over hot spots in the middle of a plate instead volcanoes are dangerous because of lava flows ash clouds that can stop planes and pyroclastic flows which are fast avalanches of hot gas and ash but they also create new land and very fertile soil which is why many farmers live near them and scientists watch for small earthquakes ground swelling and gas changes to warn people before an eruption alright that is it for today drop your questions below and see you next week
keyPoints: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust where molten rock, gas and ash escape.
Magma is molten rock underground that rises because it is lighter and collects in a magma chamber; on the surface it is called lava.
Eruptions happen when dissolved gases in rising magma form bubbles and pressure builds until magma bursts out.
Runny low-gas magma gives gentle lava eruptions, while thick gassy magma gives explosive eruptions.
Most volcanoes form where tectonic plates meet, such as the Ring of Fire, and some form over hot spots.
Volcanoes are dangerous because of lava, ash and pyroclastic flows, but they create fertile soil, and scientists monitor earthquakes and gas to warn people.
